MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 9, 2021
Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities this Council Meeting was
conducted via Video Teleconferencing for all Council and Staff with the exception of the City
Attorney and City Clerk who were present in the Council Chamber. All public comments that
were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the meeting.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at
5:01 p.m., on February 9, 2021, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on February 4, 2021, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Teleconferenced:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Teleconferenced:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services

Staff Present:  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation: Initiation of Litigation
  Pursuant to Paragraph (4) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 (2 cases)

City Council Minutes  1  February 9, 2021
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley stated there was one Closed Session with two components and that the
City Council was updated but no reportable actions occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Goodell

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize Director of Community Relations Karen Hamman on her Retirement

  Mayor Kelley presented a proclamation to Director of Community Relations Karen
  Hamman.

P2. School Spotlight - Capistrano Valley High School

  Received presentation from Principal John Misustin.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Annie Cwieka, M.V.: Thanked the Mayor and City Attorney for their work to developing guidelines
aimed at prohibiting sidewalk vendors from displaying profanity laced messages.

Jonathan Hawes: Commented on the $10 million embezzlement from the El Monte Promise
Foundation Scholarship Fund in the City of El Monte and asked that the City Council call out these
crimes. He states that documentation with the District Attorney’s Office are available to the public
online.

Casey Ackerman, M.V.: Stated that the enforcement of vulgarity and ADA issues related to
sidewalk vendors has fallen short and that Senate Bill 946 protecting sidewalk vendors does allow
for local cities to require permits and other steps. He encourages the city to face this problem head
on to the fullest extent possible.

Walter Lawson, M.V.: Asked if the City Council Members would consider an election to permit
citizens to vote on district-based elections.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
City Council Minutes  2  February 9, 2021
 AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of January 26, 2021, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated January 15, 2021 in the Amount of $3,032,439.46

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated January 22, 2021 in the Amount of $630,552.84

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for December 2020

  Received and filed.

5.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for December 2020

  Received and filed.

6.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for December 2020

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for December
  2020

  Received and filed.

8.  Transmittal of Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the quarter ending December 31, 2020

  Received and filed the accompanying Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the Quarter ending

9.  Coronado Park Play Area Rehabilitation - (CIP 328)

  Awarded a contract for Coronado Park Play Area Rehabilitation design services and
  preparation of construction drawings to LandStudio360 in an amount not to exceed

City Council Minutes  3  February 9, 2021
 10. Orange County Operational Area Agreement

  Approved the Orange County Operational Area Agreement.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

11. Investment Advisory Commission Appointment

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum to
  appoint Arthur Levine to the Investment Advisory Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

12. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  No report was given.

13. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Goodell.

STAFF REPORTS

14.  2021-2023 Pre-Budget Discussion

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas gave the staff report.

  Adi Mitchell, M.V.: Outlined the proposed events that the Mission Viejo Activities
  Committee proposes for 2021 and 2022 once the COVID restrictions are fully lifted.

  Nic Hernandez, M.V.: Thanked the City Council for their hard work during these
  unprecedented times. Asked that the budget item regarding “Marty Russo Youth Athletic
  Parks: Add additional ballfield lights” be moved up on the budget list.

  Garrett Mitton, M.V.: Asked that the City Council consider moving up the “Marty Russo
  Youth Athletic Parks: Add additional ballfield lights” on the budget list. Stressed that this
  lights project gives all our kids more time to achieve aspects of life that we have sorely
  missed due to the pandemic.

  Council Member asked various questions regarding the budget and by consensus received
  the report.

City Council Minutes  4  February 9, 2021
 CITY MANAGER REPORT

City Manager Dennis Wilberg highlighted that the City has 44 employees signed up for the
County’s volunteer portal and that half of them have already put in volunteer time at Soka
University. He stressed that the difficulty is not the lack of locations for the vaccine, it is the supply
of the availability of the vaccine.

CITY ATTORNEY REPORT

City Attorney Bill Curley reiterated that he does not have the power to create or impose any
licensing program. This is a legislative decision. The City has historically been business
supportive. He stated that the City has not imposed any business license tax, business permits,
business licensing as a cost item which has been consistent for the City’s entire existence. The
State’s narrow allocation of the City’s power to create or impose a permit would in no way prohibit,
limit or control sidewalk vendors, but would create a new cost and management obligation for City
staff. There is a reasonable argument that the city could not create a business permit only for one
class of business, it would need to encompass all businesses. Lastly, he stressed that this is a State
Law that is imposed on the City and that we are doing everything legally that we can.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

15. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell mentioned that he is very busy with the Orange County Transportation
Agency (OCTA) meetings and that he was appointed to the Board of Directors for the Orange
County Council of Government (OCCOG). He attended the Orange County Business Council
Installation dinner via Zoom but was unable to keep a good connection so he missed a lot of the
program. Council Member Goodell stated that he and Council Member Sachs are working
together on the Economic Development Committee along with several staff members.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths thanked the Mayor for everything she is doing. He attended the
DayBreakers this morning via Zoom. The small businesses of the City appreciate everything our
City Council is doing. Council Member Raths gave a shout out to Chamber CEO Doug Zielasko.
Lastly, he stated he is praying that we can start to get back to normal and get through this pandemic.

Council Member Sachs

16. City Support for Local Businesses: Grant Program, Coupons, and Other Options

  Council Member Sachs presented his report.
City Council Minutes  5  February 9, 2021
   Braden Swope, M.V.: Voiced in favor of the coupon program and asked for more details.
  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Raths to (1) direct
  staff to develop and maintain a citywide business inventory; (2) appropriate funding in the
  amount of $350,000 for local business support; and (3) direct staff to continue researching
  coupon promotional efforts.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum encourage residents to shop locally. She mentioned with the housing
allocation that there will be one more meeting with the appeals board next week on February 16
where the decision on the appeals that were completed and the distribution out to the region with
the reductions that were made which were under 3,000 units. She wanted to remind residents how
the state is tying our hands regarding housing allocations and the affordability factor they are
imposing us. Mayor Pro Tem reiterated that the City is doing everything we can as we approach
the year with our planning process. Lastly, she quoted keynote speaker Sully from the Orange
County Business Council meeting “Courage is Contagious and Just good enough isn’t.” and
announced that the Character Word of the Month for February is Unity.

Mayor Kelley

17. A Resolution of The City Council of The City of Mission Viejo (1) Announcing Its
  Commitment to End Child Marriage by Calling for An "18 No Exceptions" Law; And
  (2) Authorizing The City Manager And Authorized City Personnel To Publish On The
  City’s Website Necessary Information Pertaining To Ending Child Marriage

  Mayor Kelley presented her report.

  The following spoke in support of adoption of this resolution to end child marriages in
  California under the age of 18. Nesha Abiraj, Rima Nashashibi, Sara Tasneem, and Elizabeth
  Sitton.

  Council Member Goodell stated that he is struggling with the wording of “No Exceptions
  under 18”. He indicated that his mother married his father when she was 17 and his father
  was 19. They had a very successful marriage and entered it freely. He feels there could be
  exceptions.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum to adopt Resolution
  21-03 (1) Announcing Its Commitment to End Child Marriage by Calling for an “18 No
  Exceptions” Law; and (2) Authorizing the City Manager and Authorized City Personnel to
  Publish on the City’s Website and Social Media Platforms Necessary Information Pertaining
  to Ending Child Marriage.
City Council Minutes  6  February 9, 2021
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  Goodell
  ABSENT:  None

Mayor Kelley stated that she also attended the Orange County Business Council virtual meeting.
She addressed the concerns of residents that are trying to get their COVID vaccination that the
process is slow but is working and to be patient. Mayor Kelly mentioned that the City has offered
to host a vaccination clinic through Supervisor Lisa Bartlett’s Office at the community center and
the desire to have mobile clinics at Casta del sol and Palmia. She reiterated what City Manager
Dennis Wilberg said, that the problem is not the availability of sights but the availability of
vaccines. As more vaccines become available we will see more clinics opening up. Mayor Kelley
stressed the importance of supporting our local businesses. She thanked Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
for her shout out of our character word of Unity this month and she encourages residents to join the
Community of Character Committee. She stated that the committee meets twice a month at 5:30
and the committee is comprised of mostly 8th grade and high school students. At the present time
there are approximately 25-30 8th grade and high school students and 7 adults. Mayor Kelley
indicated that one of their most recent accomplishments was implementing a tutoring program
online for students.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:01 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, February 23, 2021, at 5:00 p.m.

Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 23, 2021

City Council Minutes  7  February 9, 2021
